name: Schneider Electric
description: Supplies power management and cooling systems for data centres.
operations: Global equipment provider; a location marker does not identify a particular customer.
prompt: Does the efficiency claim include the whole facility and its energy source?

name: ASML
description: Makes lithography equipment used to manufacture chips.
operations: R&D/manufacturing in the Netherlands, US, Germany and Asia; selected sites shown in operations view.
prompt: Where do components come from, and which sales require licences?

name: Tokyo Electron
description: Supplies semiconductor production equipment.
operations: Equipment and service business across chipmaking markets.
prompt: Which processing steps depend on imported equipment?

name: NVIDIA
description: Designs GPUs and supplies the CUDA software platform.
operations: Chip manufacturing is performed by partners; selected TSMC production is documented separately.
prompt: Does software lock-in matter as much as the price of hardware?

name: TSMC
description: Contract foundry manufacturing chips for other companies.
operations: Headquarters in Taiwan; selected Arizona manufacturing shown separately.
prompt: Where are fabrication and packaging actually performed?

name: SK hynix
description: Makes memory, including high-bandwidth memory used in AI computing.
operations: Icheon and Cheongju fabrication; overseas sites are not exhaustively mapped.
prompt: Could a memory or packaging bottleneck constrain deployment?

name: Arm
description: Provides processor architecture and design technology.
operations: Global offices and technology licensing; manufacturing is a separate activity.
prompt: Who owns the design rights and controls the licence?

name: Amazon Web Services
description: Cloud infrastructure and managed AI services.
operations: Global cloud regions; consult the live region list for any specific workload.
prompt: Which region runs the workload and who controls encryption keys?

name: OVHcloud
description: Cloud infrastructure with GPU services for AI.
operations: International data centres; headquarters and compute location are distinct.
prompt: Can the customer move its models and data to another provider?

name: Alibaba Cloud
description: Cloud infrastructure with locations across multiple markets.
operations: Operating cloud regions are listed separately from announced regions.
prompt: Which service region and legal entity actually handle the data?

name: Appen
description: Provides human-supported AI data collection, annotation and evaluation.
operations: Corporate HQ Sydney; US HQ Kirkland; offices listed in the UK, China, Japan, the Philippines, India and Vietnam.
prompt: How are task rates, rejected work and worker appeals handled?

name: Sama
description: Provides human-verified data annotation and evaluation.
operations: Documented teams in Kenya and Uganda. In 2026 Meta ended an annotation contract after reporting on smart-glasses footage, and Sama issued 1,108 redundancy notices. Earlier, Sama workers labelled harmful text for OpenAI.
prompt: Can workers verify pay, monitoring and grievance claims?

name: Common Crawl
description: Makes web crawl datasets available for research and other uses.
operations: The corpus is global; a US organizational base does not describe the origins of all data.
prompt: Which sites, languages and rights are included or excluded?

name: Masakhane
description: Grassroots research community for African-language NLP.
operations: Distributed participants; no single headquarters is assigned.
prompt: Who decides language priorities, and who owns the resulting resources?

name: OpenAI
description: Develops AI models, APIs and ChatGPT.
operations: Products and research reach many markets; a base marker does not locate every inference request.
prompt: Which model/version, data practices and evaluations support the claim?

name: Anthropic
description: Develops Claude models, products and safety research.
operations: Multi-cloud: AWS is its primary training and cloud provider; it also announced up to one million Google TPUs (October 2025) and a $30 billion Azure commitment on NVIDIA systems (November 2025).
prompt: How much control rests with cloud partners and model operators?

name: Google DeepMind
description: AI research organization developing models and scientific applications.
operations: Part of Google; research teams and deployment infrastructure span countries.
prompt: Who can independently reproduce a scientific or benchmark claim?

name: Mistral AI
description: Develops AI models and services, including Le Chat.
operations: Model access and licence terms vary by release; check the specific model card.
prompt: Is this an open-weight release, an API service or both?

name: DeepSeek
description: Develops language models, chat and API services.
operations: Service operator is Hangzhou DeepSeek; downloaded weights and hosted services have different data flows.
prompt: Is the story about model weights or the hosted application?

name: Sarvam AI
description: Develops text, speech and language AI for Indian languages.
operations: Bengaluru address; multilingual models and APIs serve Indian-language use cases.
prompt: What do independent tests show for dialects and code-switching?

name: AI Singapore / SEA-LION
description: Develops multilingual models and evaluation resources for Southeast Asia.
operations: Regional language coverage; the program is based in Singapore.
prompt: Which languages and cultural contexts are tested by local speakers?

name: Technology Innovation Institute
description: Applied research institute associated with the Falcon model family.
operations: UAE research base; availability and licences depend on the model release.
prompt: What can outside researchers inspect and reproduce?

name: CENIA / LatamGPT
description: AI research centre coordinating a Latin American language-model initiative.
operations: Latam-GPT launched in February 2026: a 70-billion-parameter model adapted from Meta’s Llama 3.1 and reportedly trained on AWS. Chilean coordination is not the location of every contributor.
prompt: Who contributed the corpus, and how are regional communities represented?

name: Lelapa AI
description: Builds multilingual speech and translation tools, including Vulavula.
operations: Focus on African-language and code-switching use cases; no city-level HQ claim here.
prompt: Can performance be verified on real local-language calls?

name: Hugging Face
description: Hosts models, datasets and developer collaboration tools.
operations: International platform and community; hosted repositories have their own licences.
prompt: Does a repository licence cover its data as well as its weights?

name: PyTorch Foundation
description: Supports the PyTorch machine-learning software ecosystem.
operations: Under the Linux Foundation; development is distributed internationally.
prompt: Who funds maintenance and can users reproduce or audit the code?

name: DeepL
description: Provides translation, writing and language-service interfaces.
operations: Cologne registered office; users and product availability span markets.
prompt: Which text is retained, and where do translation errors affect meaning?

name: Mila
description: Nonprofit AI research institute bringing together university researchers.
operations: Montréal research base; international collaborations.
prompt: How do sponsor funding and compute access shape research priorities?

name: RIKEN R-CCS
description: Research centre for computational science and supercomputing.
operations: Kobe centre; public scientific computing serves multiple fields, including AI research.
prompt: Who receives allocations and what research can the public inspect?

name: LNCC / Santos Dumont
description: National scientific computing laboratory hosting Santos Dumont.
operations: Brazilian research computing infrastructure; not exclusively an AI facility.
prompt: How much public compute is available to researchers beyond major cities?

name: Data Science Nigeria
description: Builds AI skills, research and social-impact applications.
operations: Lagos research centre and broader training activity; international collaborations.
prompt: Who gains skills and access, and what benefits are measured?

name: CSIRO
description: Australia’s national science agency conducts AI research and applied work.
operations: Multiple Australian sites; marker represents the agency rather than a particular lab.
prompt: What problem, validation and public benefit justify the project?

name: UNESCO
description: Publishes a global recommendation on AI ethics.
operations: International membership; an ethical recommendation is distinct from domestic enforcement.
prompt: Who translates the principles into funded and enforceable practice?

name: OECD.AI
description: Provides AI policy analysis, principles and incident resources.
operations: Intergovernmental work; member coverage is not universal global representation.
prompt: Whose incidents and national experiences are visible in the data?

name: European Commission / AI Office
description: EU institutions implement and coordinate the AI Act framework.
operations: The AI Act applies in phases: general-purpose AI model rules since August 2025 and transparency duties since August 2026. The 2026 Digital Omnibus moved high-risk rules to 2 December 2027 (stand-alone) and 2 August 2028 (in regulated products).
prompt: Which obligation applies, who supervises it, and what evidence exists?

name: NIST
description: Publishes the voluntary AI Risk Management Framework.
operations: US standards institute; voluntary use is distinct from a binding legal requirement.
prompt: Is the company reporting actual controls or only claiming alignment?

name: AlgorithmWatch
description: Investigates automated systems and their effects on society.
operations: European civil-society work; it is not a regulator.
prompt: Who can investigate systems that companies keep opaque?

name: TÜBİTAK ULAKBİM / TRUBA
description: Provides national research computing, including ARF and the ARF-ACC GPU cluster.
operations: Published ARF-ACC queue documentation lists NVIDIA H100/H200 hardware.
prompt: Who gets GPU time, how long are queues, and which suppliers support the cluster?

name: Turkcell
description: Operates domestic data-centre/cloud infrastructure and has a planned Google Cloud region partnership.
operations: Existing infrastructure differs from the planned Google region, which Turkcell estimates will operate in 2028-2029; Turkcell plans to invest $1 billion in data centres and cloud.
prompt: Which capacity is live, and which part is an investment commitment?

name: T3 Foundation / T3 AI
description: Turkish-language model and community initiative led by T3 Foundation and developed with Baykar.
operations: The foundation describes an open-source project; inspect release artefacts before treating that as a licence classification.
prompt: What data, weights, code and evaluation are actually available?

name: HAVELSAN / MAIN
description: Provides the MAIN enterprise AI platform, including deployment on closed networks.
operations: Company markets domestic AI capabilities; the claim does not establish a wholly domestic supply chain.
prompt: Which components are developed locally, licensed or imported?

name: SESTEK
description: Develops conversational automation and speech technology.
operations: Turkish operating base; part of Unifonic, illustrating ownership beyond the local ecosystem.
prompt: Where are models, customer recordings and ownership decisions located?

name: Boğaziçi University / BOUN Treebank
description: University research includes manually annotated Turkish-language resources.
operations: BOUN Treebank is a documented research resource; the cited paper is historical, not a 2026 release claim.
prompt: Who annotates Turkish data, and what licence and coverage limits apply?

name: Türkiye AI Initiative (TRAI)
description: Connects businesses, provides training and maintains an AI startup map.
operations: A commercial ecosystem platform, not an independent regulator; its directory is a discovery tool.
prompt: Does being listed establish deployment, revenue or original model development?

name: KVKK
description: Türkiye’s personal-data protection authority publishes guidance on generative AI.
operations: Personal-data oversight; guidance must be distinguished from statutory obligations and decisions.
prompt: Where is personal data sent, and what lawful basis and remedy exist?

name: Ministry of Industry and Technology
description: Coordinates industrial technology policy and the Türkiye AI Action Plan (2026-2030).
operations: The plan entered into force through Presidential Circular 2026/9 (Official Gazette, 18 August 2026). Targets are commitments, not evidence of delivery.
prompt: Which budgets, responsible agencies, milestones and progress reports back the plan’s targets?

name: Statkraft
description: Offers renewable electricity and site solutions for data centres.
operations: Norwegian site offerings and power-market activities; no named customer dependency is inferred.
prompt: Does the renewable claim describe annual certificates or hourly power matching?

name: Glencore
description: Produces and markets metals including copper and cobalt.
operations: Global mining and commodity activities; inclusion illustrates material foundations, not supply to a named AI vendor.
prompt: Can a particular material be traced from a mine to this infrastructure?

name: Google / Google Cloud
description: Designs TPU accelerators, sells cloud capacity and develops Gemini models; parent of Google DeepMind.
operations: Cloud regions worldwide, including a planned Türkiye region with Turkcell. TPUs are Google-designed chips made by partner foundries.
prompt: Which workloads run on Google’s own chips, and which on rented NVIDIA hardware?

name: Meta
description: Publishes Llama open-weight models and runs social platforms and AI-enabled devices.
operations: Llama weights come with Meta’s own licence terms, which models built on them inherit. Human review of device data has involved outsourced annotators.
prompt: Which licence terms and data practices travel with a model built on Llama?

name: Huawei (Ascend)
description: Designs Ascend AI processors and sells AI computing systems and cloud services.
operations: On the US Entity List since 2019; 2025 US guidance warns that using certain Ascend chips anywhere may breach US export controls. Illustrates a parallel chip ecosystem.
prompt: Which export rules, suppliers and software stack does a non-NVIDIA alternative depend on?

name: TÜBİTAK BİLGEM / BİLGE
description: TÜBİTAK’s informatics institute develops BİLGE, a Turkish large-language-model family unveiled in June 2026.
operations: TÜBİTAK said in June 2026 that BİLGE was not yet a public service. Parameter counts and benchmark claims in media reports differ and are not independently verified.
prompt: Which BİLGE models, training data, evaluations and access terms are actually published?
